questions.q: What are the five beats of this capstone's presentation story arc, in order?
options: Business problem, architecture, build, production practices, results
Architecture, build, business problem, results, production practices
Only architecture and build — the rest is optional
Results, then a live demo, then the business problem
questions.explain: The lesson lays out the arc in the exact order the capstone was built: problem, architecture, build, production practices, then results.

questions.q: According to the lesson, where do most candidates stop in telling this project's story, and why is that a problem?
options: They stop at the build (step 3), skipping production practices and results — which are what separate a tutorial from a job-ready project
They stop at the business problem and never explain the architecture
They over-explain results without ever mentioning the architecture
There is no common stopping point among candidates
questions.explain: The guide is explicit: most candidates stop at step 3 (the build), missing the production-practices and results beats that prove job-readiness.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend showing live during an interview demo?
options: The CloudWatch dashboard (northfield-pipeline-dashboard) and a fast Athena query against curated data
The full raw IAM policy JSON, scrolled through line by line
The GitHub Actions workflow YAML file
The complete Step Functions ASL definition, read aloud
questions.explain: The dashboard and a fast Athena query are recommended as live demos because they're visual, fast, and reliably legible under interview pressure.

questions.q: Why does the lesson suggest describing the Step Functions graph and IAM JSON from a diagram instead of live in the console?
options: Live console access during an interview is unpredictable, and dense JSON is easier to walk through verbally with a diagram than scrolled through live
AWS prohibits showing IAM policies during interviews
Step Functions graphs cannot be viewed in the console at all
It's illegal to demo Step Functions state machines externally
questions.explain: The guide's reasoning is practical: console demos of dense content are unpredictable and hard to follow live, so a diagram plus verbal walkthrough communicates better.

questions.q: What kind of answer does the lesson recommend for the 'what would you do differently at scale?' question, versus what to avoid?
options: Specific answers already reasoned through in earlier lessons (e.g. DMS for CDC, Redshift concurrency scaling), rather than a generic answer like 'add more monitoring'
Refusing to answer, since scale questions are unfair
Claiming the current build already handles unlimited scale with no changes needed
A completely different project than the one just presented
questions.explain: The lesson recommends drawing on specific, already-reasoned trade-offs from Lessons 3-13 rather than a vague, generic response.
